test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 28 July, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Arrange the parts to form a correct sentence:

P: despite being accused

Q: they

R: remained silent

S: of misconduct
solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3)** i.e. **PSQR**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the introductory phrase "Despite being accused," which is **part (P).**
 
• In English grammar, the verb "accused" is idiomatically followed by the preposition "of." This creates a logical mandatory pair between **part (P)** and **part (S)** ("of misconduct").
 
• Following the introductory dependent clause (PS), the main clause must start with a subject. **Part (Q)** "they" serves as the subject of the sentence.
 
• **Part (R)** "remained silent" provides the predicate (action) for the subject, completing the thought logically and grammatically.

Therefore, the correct sequence is **PSQR**, forming the sentence: *"Despite being accused of misconduct, they remained silent."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (PQRS):** This sequence places "they remained silent" between "accused" and "of misconduct," which breaks the grammatical link of the phrasal verb "accused of."
 
• **Option 2 (QRPS):** Although "They remained silent despite being accused of misconduct" is a grammatically valid sentence, in standardized tests, the structure beginning with the introductory phrase (PSQR) is typically favored to test clause recognition.
 
• **Option 4 (QSPR):** This arrangement is nonsensical as it places "of misconduct" immediately after the subject "they" without a connecting verb or context.
